An army marches on its stomach (and so does a family)

Ask anyone about their favourite day out and food will come up within about thirty seconds. Fish and chips on the harbour wall, a Sunday roast in a country pub, a doughnut on the pier, a proper ice cream in a cone – the food is often the bit you remember most. Getting it right means planning a little, so nobody ends up hangry in a queue for overpriced sandwiches.

Classic day-out food stops

  • The chippy – the seaside essential. Whitby, Scarborough, Cleethorpes and Grimsby, Britain's famous fishing town, all take their fish and chips very seriously.
  • Country pubs – hearty meals, beer gardens and often dog-friendly, great after a walk.
  • Cafés and tearooms – cream teas, cakes and light lunches, especially around heritage sites and market towns.
  • Ice cream parlours – family-run parlours on the coast are a holiday ritual.
  • Street food and markets – food halls and markets in cities and seaside towns offer something different for every member of the group.
  • Takeaways – pizza, kebabs and curries for a relaxed night back at the caravan or hotel.
  • Local specialities – Cornish pasties, Whitstable oysters, Bakewell puddings and Lincolnshire sausages are worth seeking out.

Choosing where to eat

With kids, look for a children's menu, high chairs and quick service. Groups should book ahead on weekends, as popular pubs and restaurants fill quickly. If anyone in your party has allergies or dietary needs, check menus online and ring ahead; by law, food businesses must be able to tell you about the main allergens in their dishes. For accessibility, ask about step-free entrances and accessible toilets, as older pubs and cafés can be tricky.

Hungry tips

  • Eat early or late – noon to 2pm is peak time everywhere.
  • Pack snacks to keep everyone going between meals.
  • Bring a picnic for one meal and treat yourselves for the other.
  • Follow the locals – a queue of people in work clothes usually means it's good.
  • Book Sunday lunch well ahead at popular pubs.

Put the food stop in the right place

It is easy to spend all your time choosing the attraction and leave lunch until everybody is hungry. Have a look at the food options while you are putting the day together. A café near the beach, a chippy after the arcades or a proper sit-down meal at the end can change the whole feel of the trip.

Use the individual guide to see what sort of place you are considering, then check whether it fits around the other stops. Opening times, bookings, dietary needs and access are worth checking with the venue when they matter to your group. Some places suit a quick drink and a snack; others are somewhere to take your time. If you need the rest of the day as well, go back to the day-out ideas, seaside guides or places to stay and build from there.
